result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A gives a tighter, more concrete spec. It highlights only the changed cell, gives exact durations (1.5 s, 2 s, a 60 s marker and a 300 ms fade-out), bans loops and flashing, and uses tabular numerals to prevent layout shift. Answer B has good ideas, such as tiered importance, starred matches and a summary after the tab becomes visible again, but its timings are looser and it applies the highlight to the whole card for wickets. Both handle reduced motion and screen-reader announcements well and batch simultaneous changes reasonably. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend in-place updates, keeping the layout still, an off-screen pill, a tab-title marker and polite live regions. B is more precise: it uses tabular-nums so the digits can't shift the layout, bans looping pulses and repeated flashing outright, gives a clear timing table, says what to do when a new update arrives mid-fade, and spells out how reduced motion should behave. A adds useful ideas, such as a catch-up summary when the tab becomes visible again and starring favourite matches, but it highlights the whole card for wickets and gives less exact rules on motion and layout.
